inputs.name: ciso_assistant_version
inputs.description: Tag of the ghcr.io/intuitem/ciso-assistant-community backend and frontend images, such as "v4.1.5". Change backend_image_digest and frontend_image_digest with it.

inputs.name: backend_image_digest
inputs.description: Digest of the backend image for ciso_assistant_version. Podman pulls by the digest, so a tag that moves upstream can't change what runs.

inputs.name: frontend_image_digest
inputs.description: Digest of the frontend image for ciso_assistant_version.

inputs.name: public_url
inputs.description: The address people reach CISO Assistant at, with no path or trailing slash, such as "https://grc.example.com". The app sets its allowed host and its links from it.

inputs.name: db_host
inputs.description: Address of the PostgreSQL server, as seen from the host.

inputs.name: db_name
inputs.description: Name of the database, which has to exist already.

inputs.name: db_user
inputs.description: PostgreSQL role that owns the database.

inputs.name: db_password
inputs.description: Password of db_user. It reaches the host in root-only files and never the plan or state.

inputs.name: admin_email
inputs.description: Email address of the first administrator, who signs in with admin_password.

inputs.name: admin_password
inputs.description: Password of the first administrator. It reaches the host in a root-only file and never the plan or state. CISO Assistant sets it only when it creates the user.

inputs.name: listen_address
inputs.description: Address the web interface listens on. The default keeps it on the host for a reverse proxy in front; "0.0.0.0" listens on every address.

inputs.name: port
inputs.description: Port the web interface listens on.

inputs.name: backend_port
inputs.description: Port the API listens on, always on 127.0.0.1.

inputs.name: min_memory_mb
inputs.description: Memory, in MiB, a host needs before the circuit configures it. A 4 GB host reports a little less than 4096.

inputs.name: environment
inputs.description: More of CISO Assistant's environment variables for the backend and the worker, such as { EMAIL_HOST = "smtp.example.com", EMAIL_HOST_PASSWORD = "..." }. They go in root-only files and never reach the plan or state.
